'''Amel Ben Abda''' is a professor of mathematics at the [[National Engineering School of Tunis]]. She was the first to earn a PhD in applied mathematics in Tunisia. She is the Tunisian representative of the steering committee of the ''International Laboratory for Computer Sciences and Applied Mathematics'' on the advisory board of the ''Tunisian Woman Mathematician Association.''

== Early life and education ==
Ben Abda studied [[applied mathematics]] at the [[National Engineering School of Tunis]], graduating in 1988.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda|title=Amel Ben Abda {{!}} European Women in Mathematics|website=europeanwomeninmaths.org|language=en|access-date=2018-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713234016/http://europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda|archive-date=2018-07-13|url-status=dead}}</ref> After her degree, she worked in the [[Preparatory Institute for Engineering Studies of Nabeul]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://twma.files.wordpress.com/2016/11/bio-et-photo-amel-ben-abda-english.pdf|title=Representative of Tunisia in the Steering Committee of LIRIMA|last=|first=|date=|website=LIRIMA|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref> She went on to earn her Master's Degree in Applied Mechanics in 1988 where she also had got her PhD in Applied Mathematics in 1993.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://africanwomeninmath.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda|title=Amel Ben Abda &#124; African Women in Mathematics Association|website=Africanwomeninmath.org|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://100women.okayafrica.com/stem-articles/2018/2/28/amel-ben-adba|title=Amel Ben Adba|work=OkayAfrica's 100 Women|access-date=2018-07-13|language=en-US|archive-date=2018-06-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613161312/https://100women.okayafrica.com/stem-articles/2018/2/28/amel-ben-adba|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="TWMA">{{Cite web|url=https://twma.files.wordpress.com/2016/10/twma-celebrates-11-february.pdf|title=Tunisian Women Mathematicians' Association|last=|first=|date=2016|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref>. With that she also had an impact on the inception of the country's applied mathematics doctoral program.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twma.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/11/bio-et-photo-amel-ben-abda-english.pdf|format=PDF|title=Professor Amel Ben Abda, ENIT. ; Representative of Tunisia in the Steering Committee of LIRIMA.|website=Twma.wordpress.com|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref>  After going on to defend her habilitation in applied mathematics at the National Engineering School of Tunis in 1998. <ref name="auto"/>

== Research and career ==
In the field of [[applied mathematics]], Ben Abda has worked on a "reciprocity gap" method that can be used as an indication of defects in materials.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1993-09-01|title=The reciprocity gap: a general concept for flaws identification problems |journal=Mechanics Research Communications|language=en|volume=20|issue=5|pages=415–420|doi=10.1016/0093-6413(93)90032-J|issn=0093-6413|last1=Andrieux |first1=S. |last2=Ben Abda |first2=A. }}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Abda|first=Amel Ben|title=On the use of the Reciprocity-Gap functional in inverse scattering from planar cracks|date=2004|publisher=INRIA|url=https://hal.inria.fr/inria-00070710|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=BEN ABDA|first1=AMEL|last2=DELBARY|first2=FABRICE|last3=HADDAR|first3=HOUSSEM|title=On the Use of the Reciprocity-Gap Functional in Inverse Scattering from Planar Cracks |date=October 2005|journal=Mathematical Models and Methods in Applied Sciences|language=en|volume=15|issue=10|pages=1553–1574|doi=10.1142/s0218202505000819|s2cid=122788633 |issn=0218-2025|url=https://hal.inria.fr/inria-00070710/file/RR-5290.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Defect and material mechanics : proceedings of the International Symposium on Defect and Material Mechanics (ISDMM), held in Aussois, France, March 25-29, 2007|date=2008|publisher=Springer|others=Dascalu, Cristian; Maugin, Gérard A.; Stolz, Claude|isbn=9781402069291|location=Dordrecht|oclc=261325816}}</ref> She also works on the problem of reconstructing [[Boundary value problem|boundary conditions]] from incomplete data.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hal.tn/ProfilSite.xhtml?labo=lamsin&memberId=358|title=Profil|website=Hal.tn|access-date=2018-07-13|archive-date=2018-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713231112/http://www.hal.tn/ProfilSite.xhtml?labo=lamsin&memberId=358|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1993, Ben Abda joined the Preparatory Institute for Scientific and Technical Studies, where she was promoted to assistant professor that same year.<ref name=":1" /> In 1999 she joined the [[National Engineering School of Tunis]].<ref name=":1" /> When she defended Tunisia's first [[habilitation]] it was in 1998.<ref name=":0" /> She is responsible for the inverse theorems team at the Laboratory of Mathematical Modelling and Numeric in Engineering Sciences (LAMSIN).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lamsin.rnu.tn/presentation/membres/Amel_BEN_ABDA.htm|title=ENIT - LAMSIN|website=Lamsin.rnu.tn|access-date=2018-07-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190228084522/http://www.lamsin.rnu.tn/presentation/membres/Amel_BEN_ABDA.htm|archive-date=2019-02-28|url-status=dead}}</ref>

She is the Tunisian representative of the steering committee of the ''International Laboratory for Computer Sciences and Applied Mathematics.''<ref name=":2" /> She is on the advisory board of the ''Tunisian Woman Mathematician Association'' (TWMA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://africanwomeninmath.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda|title=Amel Ben Abda {{!}} African Women in Mathematics Association|website=Africanwomeninmath.org|language=en|access-date=2018-07-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tunwma.com/twma-advisory-members/|title=TWMA Advisory Board|date=2016-11-30|work=TUNISIAN WOMEN MATHEMATICIANS ASSOCIATION TWMA|access-date=2018-07-13|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713231337/https://tunwma.com/twma-advisory-members/|archive-date=2018-07-13|url-status=dead}}</ref> The TWMA give an annual award for the best PhD thesis in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twma.files.wordpress.com/2016/10/twma-award-for-best-phd-thesis-in-mathematics-for-women2.pdf|title=TWMA AWARD for the Best PhD Thesis in Mathematics|website=Twma.files.wordpress.com|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref>

In 1999, she published the article "Reciprocity principle and crack identification"<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://validate.perfdrive.com/fb803c746e9148689b3984a31fccd902/?ssa=21ee4e06-5ab2-4432-87dd-1bc34000af54&ssb=96611212129&ssc=https%3A%2F%2Fiopscience.iop.org%2Farticle%2F10.1088%2F0266-5611%2F15%2F1%2F010&ssi=0e71f797-cnvj-4149-9efa-8e2fdb276386&ssk=botmanager_support@radware.com&ssm=03871498228359593105325510119192&ssn=52a6503fbd2f9757c6ee019ec52f0334ab4d270d8464-99cf-4bd9-996697&sso=f3dece9d-c4170f8a09512683f12346c9711293e467941383fde1742a&ssp=87006215181783373893178333432185314&ssq=69256875041517413209250415560736671140769&ssr=MjA4LjgwLjE1NC4xMQ==&sst=Mozilla/5.0 |title=Reciprocity principle and crack identification|first1=Stéphane|last1=Andrieux|first2=Amel Ben|last2=Abda|first3=Huy Duong|last3=Bui|date=Jan 1, 1999|journal=Inverse Problems|volume=15|issue=1|pages=59–65|access-date=July 6, 2026|doi=10.1088/0266-5611/15/1/010}}</ref> with Stéphane Andrieux and Huy Duong Bui, later referring its work as here most influential and impactful research she has done on real world problems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amel Ben Abda |url=https://africanwomeninmath.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=Africanwomeninmath.org}}</ref>

In 2018 she was selected as one of [[OkayAfrica]]'s Top 100 Women.<ref name=":2" />

In 2016 she received a trophy at their annual meeting, and the trophy was for her impact on Tunisian Women that are also in the field of mathematics.<ref name="TWMA"/>

She is a prominent advocate to the Tunisian Women in Mathematics Association, she was actively a part of broader to helping with empowering other women who are also in STEM all across the continent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://africanwomeninmath.org/women-in-math/portrait/amel-ben-abda|title=Amel Ben Abda &#124; African Women in Mathematics Association|website=Africanwomeninmath.org|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref>
